articles.title: ‘I am so sorry’: Former NFL star dies tragically after concerning Facebook post
articles.summary: The NFL world is in mourning just days before the start of the 2026 season as former NFL star Alphonso Smith Jr. has tragically died at the age of 40 after a...
articles.body:
The NFL world is in mourning just days before the start of the 2026 season as former NFL star Alphonso Smith Jr. has tragically died at the age of 40 after a concerning post on Facebook.

The news comes after Smith made a Facebook post in which he referred to himself as a "coward" and said he is "so sorry."

Smith emerged as a star cornerback for the Wake Forest Demon Deacons, where he played from 2004 to 2008.

During his senior season at Wake Forest, he started all 13 games and emerged as one of the top corners in the country, earning consensus All-American honors. He was also one of five finalists for the Bronko Nagurski Trophy and continues to hold the ACC record for interceptions in a career with 21.

Following his standout college football career, Smith was selected with the No. 37 overall pick by the Denver Broncos. After spending the 2009 season with the Broncos, he was traded to the Detroit Lions, where he played from 2010 to 2012 when his football career came to an end.

According to a report from TMZ Sports , Smith took his own life at a housing community in Florida after posting a concerning message on Facebook.

"Do not cry for me! I tried everything in my power to fight the demons behind the ones that someone put into ME! I did not want to be that WAY! I know I have disappointed so many folks. This is a DEMON in me! But not only me! It's EVERYONE! I have HURT so many! I needed help & did not get it! I am so sorry! I am a piece of sh*t! It's a lot of you that are! I am A COWARD! A HUGE COWARD! I am so sorry…

"To my kids, daddy is SO SORRY! To my friends, I love you all, but your boy was f*cked up! To my family, BABY, my MOM, my siblings, things happened to your boy, your brother while I was little that an older lady did onto me. As a result guys, I did the same onto others! Please forgive me!

"Please pray over your families! PLEASE PRAY FOR ALL I've affected! I am the WORST & I pray my soul rest in heaven for my heart is pure, but my BRAIN & experience is MESSED UP!!"

Smith ended his letter with "I'm SORRY! THIS IS IT!"

If you or someone you know is struggling or in crisis, help is available. Call or text 988 or chat 988lifeline.org.

articles.title: Marc Marquez given brutal warning ahead of Pedro Acosta Ducati showdown
articles.summary: Marc Marquez could be facing the toughest task of his career when he faces up against Pedro Acosta at Ducati next season. That’s according to his former titl...
articles.body:
Marc Marquez could be facing the toughest task of his career when he faces up against Pedro Acosta at Ducati next season.

That's according to his former title rival, Andrea Dovizioso, who sees the pairing as unlike anything Marquez has experienced before .

The nine-time champion will be joined in Italy by Acosta next season after the pair signed contracts with Ducati for 2027 and 2028.

Acosta is yet to win a MotoGP race, but is a champion in Moto2 and Moto3, and has thrilled ever since he stepped up to the premier class with KTM.

The deal has whetted the appetites of many, and also provoked some to question whether it could signal that Marquez's legendary career is coming to an end.

Acosta and Marquez are all smiles now, but that could change next season (Credit: Red Bull Content Pool)

It's also prompted comparisons to when Valentino Rossi was joined by Jorge Lorenzo at Yamaha in 2008, creating a two-pronged attack of elite riders and an almighty rivalry.

However, Dovizioso has explained why the analogy isn't quite right.

Marc Marquez and Acosta pairing compared to Rossi vs Lorenzo

"Marc isn't in the same situation as Valentino. Valentino, however, was still at the top," he said on the podcast 04 bar.

"Yes, he wasn't so young anymore, but he'd been there for many years. Marc isn't in that situation; physically, he has too many problems."

Marquez prompted retirement fears earlier this season when he fractured his ankle at Le Mans and was caught in tears as he explained the pain in his shoulder.

A double surgery has eased the pain, but the 33-year-old has been to hell and back with arm issues, going through seven operations since 2020 and missing numerous races.

Dovizioso thinks it's clear he can no longer race at his peak, nor hide those struggles from his rivals.

Dovizioso says Marquez can no longer hide physical limitations

He explained: "He's not just upset, he's desperate.

"Now he's not hiding it anymore, because, after all, he's a strategist and he's tried to downplay his limitations while he could, but they were so obvious that now they're plain for all to see.

"As a strategist, why show an expression of total exhaustion after a race where you suffered a lot and had no control over your body? He said that.

"It's the worst thing you can tell your rival, but that expression, when he describes those sensations, you see there's nothing [left] to interpret..."

It's not just Marquez's physical limitations, though, but Acosta's talent that has Dovizioso questioning how things will play out at Ducati next season.

Last time out in Aragon, Marquez won the race , but Acosta followed him home in second on a KTM whose development has been halted as the manufacturer instead focuses on the 2027 regulation changes.

Dovizioso intrigued by 'real Acosta' at Ducati

"In my opinion, there's still a lot to discover about Acosta in many aspects, despite all the extraordinary things he's already done. Both in terms of his character and his behaviour," Dovizioso said.

"We don't know him very well because he's young and he's going to change teams; it's the first time he's racing a different bike with a specific team, as Marc's teammate.

"It will be an interesting situation and we'll soon start to discover the real Acosta. Right now it's a little difficult."

images.caption: Acosta and Marquez are all smiles now, but that could change next season (Credit: Red Bull Content Pool)

articles.title: 2026 Week 1 Preview: Oregon State Beavers @ Houston Cougars
articles.summary: Houston and Oregon State open on ESPN in a rematch of a 2025 Friday night thriller.
articles.body:
Time and date: Saturday, September 5 at 12:00 p.m. ET

Last meeting: Houston 27, Oregon State 24 — September 26, 2025

A different energy resonates throughout the air in Houston, TX.

For the first time since joining the Big 12, the Houston Cougars enter a season with expectations. Ranked No. 23 in the AP Poll, they enter with their highest preseason ranking since 2016. Fresh off a 10-win season, the Cougars retained head coach Willie Fritz, all three coordinators, and many of last year's top contributors. Fritz orchestrated a rapid rise from the cellar of the Big 12, and now the pieces are in place for conference championship contention.

Oregon State hopes to engineer a similar turnaround in Corvallis. The Beavers enjoyed considerable success in the early 2020s, but the program took a dramatic step backward when the classic iteration Pac-12 dissolved. After stumbling to 2-10 in 2025, Oregon State replaced head coach Trent Bray with JaMarcus Shephard, who hopes to make the Beavers a force in the revamped Pac-12.

Despite the stark contrast between their 2-10 and 10-3 records, the Beavers nearly stunned the Cougars in 2025. Houston stormed back down 14 in the final seven minutes and blocked Oregon State field goal at the buzzer to force overtime. Upon reaching the extra frame, the Cougars escaped on a walk-off field goal.

This year the series shifts to Houston, where Fritz's team enters as a significant favorite in a nationally televised showcase.

Oregon State opened the 2023 season ranked No. 18 in the AP Poll. Three years later, the program is coming off a dismal 2-10 record. The Beavers weren't as bad as their record suggested, at least during the first half of 2025. They led 9-4 Fresno State with under one minute remaining and held a 14-point fourth quarter advantage over 10-3 Houston. But the 0-7 start ultimately proved too much to overcome, as the Beavers slipped up against the likes of Tulsa and Sam Houston late in the season. Now JaMarcus Shephard aims to restore order.

One of Shephard's first major decisions involved selecting a starting quarterback. Rather than stick with incumbent Maalik Murphy, who served as Duke's starter in 2024, Shephard appointed Mercer transfer Braden Atkinson to QB1. Atkinson finished second in the FCS with 3,611 passing yards last fall, delivering 34 touchdowns against 11 interceptions on a 65.8 completion rate. He'll be tasked with improving the efficiency of a passing attack that completed only 14 touchdown passes, while tossing 13 interceptions in 2025.

Atkinson's supporting cast will look considerably different from Murphy's last year. Oregon State loses each of its top four leading receivers, and tight end Gabe Milbourn (17 receptions, 185 yards) and wide receiver Eddie Freauff (12 receptions, 144 yards) are the returning leaders in production. The Beavers turned to the portal for reinforcements, landing former Texas State receivers Aaron Butler and Xayvion Noland and Alabama transfer Aeryn Hampton, who followed new offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen from Tuscaloosa. True freshman Jesse Legree and former Central Michigan tight end DeCorion Temple could also play significant roles in an offense that ranked 18th nationally in passing attempts per game last fall.

The Beavers produced the 125th ranked scoring offense at 18.2 points per game, but one of their few bright spots was 1,000-yard rusher Anthony Hankerson. While Hankerson is gone, Oregon State can lean on Cornell Hatcher Jr., who turned in his best performance against Houston last season with 93 rushing yards and a touchdown. Vanderbilt transfer AJ Newberry also joins a running back room which possesses plenty of size. They'll run behind an offensive line returning three starters from the Trent Bray era.

Oregon State's defense played particularly well against Houston last September, but the unit lacked consistency throughout the season, allowing over 30 points in seven of 12 contests. This year's unit will operate under the direction of Mike MacIntyre, who previously served as head coach of FIU and Colorado. Despite the coaching turnover, the Beavers still retain five primary starters from 2025, headlined by middle linebacker Aiden Sullivan, the team's second-leading tackler and tackles for loss leader.

MacIntyre's defense should be strongest in the secondary. The Beavers held opposing quarterbacks to a 56.9 completion percentage a year ago and bring back cornerback Trey Glasper and nickel Sai Vadrawale, who combined for 54 tackles, 10 pass deflections, and two interceptions. TJ Crandall, who fractured his foot during fall camp last August, returns after previously last playing at West Virginia in 2024.

Forcing turnovers was a struggle for Oregon State in 2025. Sullivan forced three fumbles, but the team only recovered one all season. The Beavers finished a minus-11 in the turnover battle last year, but a plus-1 margin against Houston played a massive role in the near upset.

Houston won't sneak up on anybody this year. Opponents are well aware of the Cougars' capabilities after last sesaon's 10-3 finish. Last season, Houston was the only team to finish 6-0 on the road, yet comparatively struggled at home with a 3-3 record. The Cougars emerged victorious in six of seven one-score games, hoping that statistic proves sustainable, rather than an anomaly that could regress to the mean.

Returning an established starting quarterback is always a plus, and Houston has that in Conner Weigman. In his first year as a Cougar, the former 5-star Texas A&M recruit produced 2,705 yards, 25 touchdowns, and nine interceptions. However, the reigning Texas Bowl MVP — who regularly dealt with lower-body injuries at his previous stop — surprised many defenses with his mobility. Weigman eclipsed 80 rushing yards in six games, including three outings with at least 110. Although Houston landed the No. 1 quarterback recruit in the country in Keisean Henderson this offseason, Weigman retains his starting duties as a fifth-year senior.

Houston's offense also returns Amare Thomas. The First Team All-Big 12 wide receiver is the conference's returning leader in receiving yards (966) and touchdowns (12). Thomas dominated the production at the position in 2025, as no other Cougar wide receiver recorded more than 13 catches or 275 yards. The group should be deeper this year thanks to the combined development of Koby Young and Harvey Broussard, and the arrivals of transfers Tyson Turner (Texas Tech) and Trent Walker (Oregon State). Saturday will be an emotional game for Walker, who faces his former team after producing consecutive 800+ yard seasons in Corvallis.

The Cougars lose a near-1,000-yard rusher in Dean Connors but reload with Makhi Hughes, who surpassed 1,300 yards in consecutive seasons at Tulane. The former Green Wave star reunites with Willie Fritz, although he eyes a bounce-back season after being underutilized at Oregon in 2025. Hughes will be supported by his former star guard Shadre Hurst. One of the most coveted portal additions this offseason, Hurst arrives as an AP First Team Preseason All-American selection, while boasting some of the most impressive weight-room numbers among FBS linemen. Two former All-MAC stars — center Anthony Boswell and right tackle Drew Terrill — also join a restructured Houston line that ranked in the top 30 in fewest sacks allowed last year.

Houston fielded a solid defense overall in coordinator Austin Armstrong's first year at the helm. Now Armstrong's unit enters 2026 with a healthy mix of returning talent and transfers. While the Cougars lose tackles leader Carlos Allen and sacks leader Eddie Walls on the defensive line, they replace them with substantially more size. Ashton Porter arrives from Oregon as a 6'3", 280-pound defensive end, while defensive tackles Ejiro Egodogbare (6'3", 310) and De'Marion Thomas (6'2", 340) bolster the interior. The front also returns contributors such as Khalil Laufau, who dominated in the Texas Bowl last December, and Brandon Mack II, the team's returning sacks leader with 5.0.

The linebacking corps retains Sione Fotu and adds transfer Jaden Yates, a former First Team All-Sun Belt selection at Marshall who started nine games for a College Football Playoff-caliber Ole Miss team. The secondary offers more continuity, retaining All-Big 12 cornerback Will James and both starting safeties, Kentrell Webb and Jordan Allen. James recorded a team-high three interceptions and broke up eight passes as a sophomore last year, and he'll be supported by new transfers. Jalen Mayo, an FCS All-American cornerback who transferred from Stephen F. Austin, occupies the other boundary corner, while Tulane transfer Javion White takes over as the nickel.

According to ESPN, Oregon State had a 99.3 percent chance of winning when Houston faced a 3rd and 17 with 6:49 remaining in last year's contest. But the Cougars staged a dramatic comeback and now enter as three-touchdown home favorites over the Beavers.

Although Houston was better on the road last season, a home opener against Oregon State should be far more manageable than last September's Friday night road trip to Corvallis. The Cougars might need time to find their offensive rhythm, as they did in Fritz's previous home openers and throughout much of their 10-3 campaign. But thanks to the advantage of their new-look offensive line, they will eventually settle in and rely on star talents like Makhi Hughes and Amare Thomas to sustain drives.

Braden Atkinson has played FBS competition before, throwing for 210 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions against Auburn last November. How he adapts in this offense, surrounded by an unproven but promising group of receivers, is the true wild card in this game.

Oregon State keeps the game competitive in the first half, but Conner Weigman and the Cougars pull away with a two-touchdown victory.

CORVALLIS, OREGON - SEPTEMBER 26: Cornell Hatcher Jr. #21 of the Oregon State Beavers runs with the ball for a touchdown during the second half against the Houston Cougars at Reser Stadium on September 26, 2025 in Corvallis, Oregon. (Photo by Soobum Im/Getty Images) | Getty Images

articles.title: Which Juventus summer signing are you most excited about?
articles.summary: Juventus, somewhat surprisingly, brought in a lot of new talent despite obvious financial restrictions. So, who you like the most out of all of them?
articles.body:
We are now two days on from the Serie A transfer window closing, and while there still can be some players outgoing to leagues who can still sign talent, the incoming player part of the equation will not happen again until January at the earliest. That means the roster is set outside of a couple of players who could still be on the way.

So, that means there's some new players still to get to know a little bit. Some very tall, others a little smaller — but not by much. All of them very much being looked at as options to help Luciano Spalletti guide this team back into the top four and qualify for the Champions League — something that would help this club out quite a bit with there only being Europa League football on the schedule this season.

But who's the most exciting of them all? Who are you, dear reader, most excited to watch in a Juventus shirt?

As a reminder since it's been such a busy couple of weeks to close out the Serie A transfer window, here are all of Juventus' summer signings:

Guglielmo Vicario (loan with option to buy)

Pape Matar Sarr (loan with option/obligation to buy)

There are permanent deals. There are loan deals. There are options to buy that come with some of those loans. There's also a dry loan for a very tall German forward who is already giving us a little bit of a laugh . There are a couple of teenagers. There's a veteran Turkish fullback who has already proven to be a solid signing that provides a nice bit of versatility. There's also a couple of goalkeepers looking to make their mark.

Oh yeah … plenty of potential reclamation prospects, too.

That's the nine-player haul that Juventus' summer mercato ended up involving. Now we get to see what they can do on the field — well, outside of Ekhator since he's current injured and out for a couple of months — as Juve try and keep this winning start to the season going as long as possible.

So, the Juventus Question of the Day is this: Of the nine players that Juventus signed during the summer transfer window, who are you most excited to watch this season (and beyond)?

articles.title: Mets Morning News: Nick Morabito’s big day lift Mets over Rays
articles.summary: Your Thursday morning dose of Mets and Major League Baseball news, notes, and links.
articles.body:
The Mets jumped out to a big lead early and then poured it on late in their bounceback victory over the Rays to take the series. Nick Morabito's first major league hit was a three-run double to help put the game out of reach. The team will now enjoy an off day before heading home to play the Giants.

Before the game the Mets reinstated Justin Hagenman from the IL and optioned Dylan Ross.

Jonah Tong turned his season around in the minors recently which has earned him a start with the big league club.

The team will have some hard decisions to make at the end of the season with some of their unproductive players.

The Mets will need to look inward to see what went wrong this year especially with former Mets finding success elsewhere.

The Braves got a much-needed 9-0 win over the Nationals.

Ronald Acuña Jr. became the fastest player in MLB history to reach 200 home runs and 200 stolen bases.

The Marlins won 9-6 in a comeback victory against the Royals.

The Phillies were shut out 1-0 by the Diamondbacks.

James Wood returned to the lineup for the Nationals after missing 27 games with an oblique strain.

The playoff race is on and the strength of schedule of those in the hunt could help decide who gets to play in October.

Baseballs are flying out of the park in the minors at an historic pace but what is behind the uptick in home runs?

Brewer's ace Jacob Misiorowski gave up five earned runs against the Cubs which ended his streak of starts allowing just three ER or less at 25.

Padres prospect Ethan Salas made his major league debut at 20 years old which made him the youngest catcher to play in a game since Ivan Rodriguez.

The Dodgers placed starter Eric Lauer on the IL with elbow inflammation after a tough start against the Cardinals.

On this date in 1965, Jim Hickman became the first Met to hit three home runs in a game .

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton pays homage to Michael Schumacher ahead of Ferrari’s Monza tribute
articles.summary: The Scuderia will sport a unique Schumacher-related livery on their car at their home event this weekend
articles.body:
Lewis Hamilton paid homage to Michael Schumacher ahead of an Italian Grand Prix weekend where Ferrari will adorn a special livery in tribute to the F1 legend.

Joining the team 30 years ago, Schumacher won five of his seven world championships at Ferrari and the prancing horse outfit announced plans earlier this week to dedicate their cars and race suits to the German legend.

The cars of Hamilton and Charles Leclerc will sport a livery inspired by the 1996 Ferrari F310, which the German drove in his debut year, and will feature hints of gold on the wheels similar to the '96 model.

The car will also feature Schumacher's logo and the seven stars that used to adorn his helmet, signifying his seven titles – a feat matched only by Hamilton. Ex-Ferrari driver Sebastian Vettel will also drive Schumacher's championship-winning 2022 car for a "celebratory" lap before Sunday's grand prix.

Asked about representing Ferrari at Monza for the second time, Hamilton said in a press conference on Thursday: "It is the best feeling, such an honour and a privilege to be a Ferrari driver. It is really phenomenal to experience it for the second year in a row."

"I haven't seen the [Schumacher] livery yet, but those seven stars that we will have, like mine, give me a good feeling."

"I always remember seeing Michael in the red car, and just trying to imagine what it would feel like to be in his shoes. He was such a leader."

While championship leader Kimi Antonelli will take a grid penalty for exceeding his engine allocation and is set to start at the back of the grid, Ferrari have brought a power unit upgrade for round 13.

"Every little helps," said Hamilton, who won his first race for Ferrari in Barcelona in June. "Even the last race, we were losing four tenths on the straight. I'm really proud of how hard everyone is working, in the factory, heads down."

"This is a step forward. It is not the whole gap we need, we knew that would be the case but just to see things coming to the car, it is exciting to see we are still pushing."

Hamilton drove into the Monza paddock on Thursday in his own recently acquired F40 car, emblazoned with his own personal number plate and, seemingly by coincidence, a "number 44 engine."

"I've been looking for one for a while, and I wanted one with low mileage," he explained. "I wanted one with a story, and lots have come up in auction over the past couple of years.

"When they took the engine out, they found out the engine's number 44, it's got stamped on the engine, number 44, I couldn't believe it.

"It feels very much fate and I thought it was a real opportunity to kind of highlight the history of Ferrari in their home country, at their race, and when am I ever going to get to do that again?"

images.caption: Lewis Hamilton arrived at Monza in his own Ferrari F40 car (Getty)
Ferrari will pay tribute to Michael Schumacher with a special livery this weekend at Monza (Scuderia Ferrari)
Hamilton poses next to his F40 car outside the Monza paddock (Getty)

articles.title: Ravens practice squad: Five players who could become contributors
articles.summary: Five young players on the Ravens' practice squad have the traits to become future contributors
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens retained several young players on their practice squad who could eventually compete for active-roster roles. Baltimore's roster is elite and built to win now, leaving limited opportunities for developmental prospects. The practice squad allows those players to improve without requiring the Ravens to sacrifice experienced depth on the 53-man roster.

Here are five prospects with the best long-term potential.

Isaac remains an intriguing pass-rushing prospect despite failing to secure an active-roster position entering his third season. Baltimore selected the former Penn State defender in the third round of the 2024 NFL draft. Injuries disrupted the beginning of his career and prevented him from establishing a consistent role.

The Ravens have significant depth on the edge, but that room could change quickly as contracts expire and veteran players age. Isaac still has an opportunity to develop into a rotational pass rusher if he remains healthy and translates his athleticism into consistent production.

Rucker has the power and physical playing style to develop into a dependable edge-setting defender. He spent the summer competing in one of Baltimore's deepest position groups. The practice squad gives Rucker additional time to expand his pass-rushing bag and improve his work on special teams. Those improvements could make him a candidate for a larger role in 2027.

Baltimore selected Benny in the seventh round before waiving him during final roster reductions. Bringing him back showed the Ravens remain interested in his development. The former Michigan defender has the size to play multiple positions along the defensive front. Learning behind Nnamdi Madubuike, Calais Campbell, Travis Jones and Broderick Washington could help Benny become more technically consistent.

At 6-foot-8 and 330 pounds, Lichtenhan has the frame NFL teams want from an offensive tackle. He also has experience in Baltimore's system after spending time with the organization in 2025. The practice squad will allow him to continue improving his balance, footwork, and hand placement. Offensive tackle is a premium position, making his development particularly valuable.

Dawkins joined the Ravens as an undrafted rookie after starting extensively at Penn State. His intelligence, toughness, and familiarity with making protection calls give Baltimore a natural developmental center. The season-ending injury to Danny Pinter demonstrated how quickly offensive line depth can disappear. Dawkins can use his rookie season to add strength and learn behind Ethan Pocic and Jovaughn Gwyn.

If he progresses, Dawkins could eventually compete for an interior reserve position that provides depth at center and guard.

articles.title: Bayern Munich’s Sacha Boey understands tough reality of his situation
articles.summary: FC Bayern has to get cracking if it wants to make a move.
articles.body:
If Bayern Munich cannot find a way to offload Sacha Boey to a league where the transfer window is still open, the right-back might have to prepare for a long season of watching from the stands per Sky Germany journalist Kerry Hau (via @iMiaSanMia ):

There were two inquiries from England for Sacha Boey on deadline day, but neither has concretized. Boey is aware that he'll most likely end up very often in the stands if he stays. The Galatasaray option is currently cold, despite reports. It remains to be seen if an option will open up for him before the transfer window shuts in other countries as well.

Boey will not be a total outcast, though, per sporting director Christoph Freund.

"Then he will be treated very fairly. He has behaved very professionally and had a good preseason," Freund told Abendzeitung journalist Kilian Kreitmair (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ).

There is still hope that Bayern Munich can find a solution, but the Bavarians might need to swallow their pride and accept a whole lot less than they originally paid for Boey. To make a deal happen, an offer of less than €10 million might have to be deemed acceptable.

articles.title: Who are the three best starting pitchers on the Red Sox right now?
articles.summary: Or perhaps even more importantly, who will the three best starting pitching options be for the Red Sox be on September 29th?
articles.body:
Here at Over The Monster, we like to ask a topical question of the day; but on this dreary morning, we might as well be asking the question of the month. Very simply: If the Wild Card series started today, who would you want starting those three games?

Of course, the Wild Card series doesn't start today, and Red Sox haven't officially punched their ticket into the dance yet. But with FanGraphs giving them a 97.1 percent chance to make the playoffs and only 0.3 percent chance to win the division as of this morning , it seems pretty darn likely they're going to be playing baseball on September 29th (and playing it somewhere other than Fenway Park).

The Red Sox know this as well and have already reshuffled their rotation to pitch Sonny Gray on Saturday (September 5th) and Payton Tolle on Sunday (September 6th). With off days for the month already scheduled for the 10th, 14th, 17th, and 28th (assuming they make the playoffs), this means Gray and Tolle could pitch with an extra day of rest every start from here to the end of the year in a normal five man rotation and be perfectly lined up to pitch Game 1 and Game 2 of the Wild Card series. (September 11th and 12th against the Royals, September 17th and 18th against the Rangers and Rays, September 23rd and 24th against the Guardians, and September 29th and 30th against the Wild Card opponent.)

So the Red Sox have already told us who they believe will start the first two games of the playoffs indirectly, but third option is far more complex. Historically, Ranger Suarez would be the best man for the job. Not only did they just give him a $130 million contract in January, but he also has a 1.48 career ERA in the playoffs. However, the Sox might not be too pleased with the way he threw the ball in Sunday's start against the Yankees with the tiebreaker on the line, and they might not want to set things up that way again for a potential winner take all game on October 1st.

So what about tonight's starter Jake Bennett? He just might be pitching for a postseason starting job over the next few weeks. If he does well and nobody steps up, the Sox could end up sending a rookie to the mound to start and do or die game in Yankee Stadium for the second year in a row.

And then there's Garrett Crochet, who won't be available to make a traditional start, but could be ramped up enough to give you a couple of innings out of the gate before you go bullpen game from there, mixing and matching the opponent with all your best arms and running their bench dry of platoon matchups by the late innings.

Those are just some of the factors on the table as we turn our eyes to the end of the month, but what does our OTM community think? Talk about this and whatever else you like, and as always, be good to one another!

images.caption: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - AUGUST 30: Ranger Suarez #55 of the Boston Red Sox pitches during the game against the New York Yankees at Yankee Stadium on August 30, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Evan Bernstein/Getty Images) | Getty Images
